A two 2 Application Development is the internally assessed unit of the A level, worth 20 percent of the qualification and taking about 60 hours. A Gantt chart lists tasks down the side and time along the top, with a bar for each task's duration. Dependencies link tasks that must happen in sequence, and milestones mark important checkpoints such as agreeing the requirements.

The critical path is the longest chain of dependent tasks: any delay on it delays the whole project. A project log records what was actually done, which helps you compare progress with the plan and explain any changes you made to it.
And is there anything people often mix up here?

Coursework must be the candidate's own work. The candidate and teacher sign declarations, and the teacher must be able to confirm that the work was produced under the required conditions. Sources, tutorials, templates and any permitted AI use must be acknowledged in the portfolio.
Okay. Keep going.

Copying, collusion or presenting generated content as your own is malpractice and can result in penalties, including disqualification. Keeping dated versions of the database and portfolio shows how the work developed over time.
Time for quickfire key terms. I'll say the term, and you give me the answer the mark scheme gives credit for.
Go for it.
Case study?
A scenario pre-released by CCEA describing an organisation's problem, which candidates analyse and solve with a database application.
Gantt chart?
A planning chart showing each task as a horizontal bar against a timeline, with durations, overlaps and dependencies.
Milestone?
A significant checkpoint in a project, such as the completion of a stage, used to monitor progress.
Dependency?
A relationship between tasks in which one task cannot start until another has been completed.
Critical path?
The longest sequence of dependent tasks in a project; a delay to any task on it delays the whole project.
Authentication?
Confirmation by the candidate and teacher that coursework is the candidate's own work, produced under the required conditions.
What about the exam? Where has this come up?

The moderator only sees your PDF, so evidence must be easy to find and clearly linked. Number your requirements and use those numbers everywhere. Show your process, not just the finished product: a design that changed, with a reason, is stronger evidence than a perfect final screenshot. Avoid unexplained screenshots and generic textbook theory copied into the portfolio; every page should be about your client's system. Read the marking grid headings and make sure each one has clearly labelled evidence.
